problems.stem: When is the method of sections usually preferable to the method of joints?
options: When you need every member force in the truss
When you need only one or a few specific member forces
When the truss has no joints
problems.explanation: The method of sections is most efficient when you want selected member forces without solving the entire truss.

problems.stem: Why is a cut through more than three unknown members usually avoided in a planar truss section analysis?
options: Because a rigid-body section still gives only three independent equilibrium equations in 2D
Because trusses cannot be cut through diagonal members
Because the method of sections ignores moments
Because all cut members must be zero-force members
problems.explanation: A planar rigid-body section gives three usable equilibrium equations, so more than three unknown cut-member forces generally makes the section unsolvable directly.

problems.stem: What is the main purpose of choosing a smart moment center in the method of sections?
options: To remove known loads from the problem
To eliminate selected unknown cut-member forces from the moment equation
To avoid drawing the free-body diagram
To convert the truss into a particle
problems.explanation: A strategically chosen moment center can make one target force solvable directly by eliminating others.

problems.stem: What should usually be solved before applying the method of sections to a truss?
options: The color code of all members
Support reactions for the whole truss
problems.explanation: Support reactions are external loads on the cut section, so they usually need to be known first.
